transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-08
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marta Diaz (Aurora Head of Product), Ethan Cole (Aurora CTO), Sophie Lin (Aurora ML Engineer)

[00:00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan with Redwood, and with me is Priya from our SE team. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:08] Marta: Doing well, thanks. Busy week but excited to see this.
[00:00:12] Ethan: Good to be here. Quick ask up front: focus on streaming and retry behavior — that's our main concern.
[00:00:20] Priya: Great, we'll cover streaming, the key params for generation (temp, top_p, max_tokens), and our retry/backoff recommendations. We'll also do a quick Console walkthrough and mention Optimize suggestions.
[00:00:30] Jordan: Agenda is short: quick qualification, then demo, then Q&A and next steps. Marta, can you give us a quick sense of Aurora's use case?
[00:00:38] Marta: Sure. We're building an internal clinician assistant for summarizing consult notes and generating suggested follow-ups. Must be HIPAA-aware, obviously. Latency needs to be sub-second for short queries, but for longer summaries 2-3s is ok. We'll start with hosted but need to know when Dedicated or Private would make sense.
[00:00:57] Sophie: And from our side, we expect bursts up to 80 qps during peak; typical prompt sizes are 150-400 tokens. We also want deterministic-ish outputs for certain templates.
[00:01:08] Priya: Helpful, thanks. The hosted API can cover those peaks with autoscaling; for strict data residency and managed KMS you might consider Dedicated or Private. We'll show where those tradeoffs live.

[00:01:30] --- Demo start ---
[00:01:30] Priya: I'm going to share my screen — bear with me while the deck loads. (screen share noise)
[00:01:45] Priya: Okay, first slide is the Redwood hosted API quickstart. We support text and chat endpoints; both support streaming. For chat we surface conversation history and role tokens.
[00:02:05] Priya: (typing) Here's a code snippet in curl for streaming: you open a chunked response, and tokens come as they generate. This helps UX because you can render partial results to the clinician UI while the server continues generation.
[00:02:25] Marta: Do you buffer on the client or do you push partial events?
[00:02:30] Priya: We stream chunks over the HTTP response as they become available; clients can either flush per-chunk or buffer a few tokens to avoid UI flicker. We recommend emitting the first partial immediately and then small buffered updates (50-100 ms) for smoother UX.
[00:02:45] Ethan: What's typical latency to first token?
[00:02:48] Priya: On our hosted fleet, for small prompts ~50-100 tokens, first token is often under 250ms in optimal regions; end-to-end depends on model and sequence. For your 150-400 token prompts, typical time-to-first-token 200-400ms and full response 600ms-2s depending on model size and config.
[00:03:10] Jordan: Note that latency varies with batching and concurrency — Optimize can suggest batching profiles to reduce cost without violating your latency SLOs.

[00:03:30] Priya: Now params: temperature controls randomness; for deterministic templates we recommend 0.0-0.2, for exploratory suggestions 0.7. Top_p can be used instead/in combination. Max_tokens caps output length — important to set per template to avoid runaway costs.
[00:03:50] Sophie: For deterministic outputs we need consistent formatting — do you support structured output or function-calling?
[00:03:57] Priya: Yes, we support structured output tooling and function calling. For templates, set low temperature, enforce stop tokens, and optionally post-process with a small validation step.

[00:04:20] Priya: Retries — important. We recommend an idempotent request pattern: include a client_request_id or idempotency_key. Our SDKs handle exponential backoff with jitter by default. For streaming specifically, if a stream fails mid-response, we surface an error and you can retry with the same idempotency key; we record partial tokens and logs for debugging.
[00:04:45] Ethan: If a mid-stream retry happens, do you dedupe duplicate outputs?
[00:04:49] Priya: We recommend the client detect partial receipts and resume pattern: either discard partial and fetch fresh, or use a resume token in planned POC protocols. Redwood's logging will show the request lifecycle so you can reconcile. Deduplication is client-handled typically.

[00:05:20] Marta: Security question: HIPAA — hosted option encrypts data at rest, but what about key management and audit logs?
[00:05:27] Jordan: Hosted encrypts data in transit and at rest, we integrate with KMS for Dedicated/Private, and we provide audit logs and event history. We'll share SOC 2 and a security whitepaper after the call. For PHI-heavy workflows many customers start hosted with a BA signed and then move to Dedicated if they need customer-managed keys.
[00:05:47] Ethan: Does hosted retain prompts or do you support no-retention?
[00:05:50] Priya: We have retention policies and can opt into no-retention for enterprise contracts. That's also a common reason customers select Dedicated/Private.

[00:06:10] Priya: Back to demo — Console quick look: Routers, per-route rate limits, trace views, and token-level cost charts. Here you can set model pins and rollout percentage for canary.
[00:06:28] Priya: (navigates) Here's the streaming logs view — you can see chunk timestamps and per-chunk latency to diagnose jitter. We've linked this to our tracing so you can correlate infra events.

[00:07:00] Sophie: For the POC, we'll want a spreadsheet of sample prompts and expected outputs to validate quality. What's the best way to run that?
[00:07:08] Jordan: We'll run a short benchmark: you send sample prompts and expected patterns, Priya will configure a run against hosted and optionally dedicated image to compare latency, cost per token, and quality metrics.

[00:07:30] --- Technical deep-dive exchange ---
[00:07:30] Ethan: On retries, do you support per-request priority or preemptive routing to reduce retry storms?
[00:07:36] Priya: We support routing policies by customer tier and route; you can set priority and reserved capacity on Dedicated. For hosted, our rate limiter and backpressure heuristics reduce retry storms. Also recommend client-side concurrency limits and exponential backoff with jitter (we provide examples).
[00:07:58] Marta: Cost: we saw a big delta between streaming small responses and full generate — how to optimize?
[00:08:05] Priya: Three levers: model choice (smaller quantized models for short replies), batching/caching (prefix cache for repeated prompts), and generation params (tight max_tokens and stop tokens). Optimize will suggest batching window sizes. For example, if you batch at 50ms you can reduce per-token compute cost up to 20-30% depending on load pattern.

[00:08:30] Priya: I'm switching to a live code sample — we'll show a Node SDK call doing streaming with a transform. (typing noise)
[00:08:45] Priya: Code shows setting stream: true, temperature: 0.1, max_tokens: 300, and a client_request_id header. On error we retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff.
[00:09:05] Sophie: If we set low temp and top_p, do you still get occasional variability?
[00:09:10] Priya: Some variability remains due to underlying sampling and tokenization differences. For absolute determinism use deterministic decoding or sequence-to-sequence templating; otherwise seed-based reproducibility isn't guaranteed across model updates. You can pin model versions to reduce drift.

[00:09:40] Jordan: Quick note on model rollouts — we recommend pinning for production and using canary routes to test new versions. Console supports A/B routing and automatic fallback if a model is underprovisioned.

[00:10:10] Muzak in background / attendee cough (audio)
[00:10:20] Marta: Sorry, distracted — quick logistics: timeline. We want a POC in two weeks and procurement by end of month if results look good.
[00:10:28] Jordan: Sounds reasonable; we'll target the POC run next week and follow up with pricing.

[00:10:40] --- Questions on SLA and Dedicated ---
[00:10:40] Ethan: For Dedicated, what's the minimum commit and typical latency SLO?
[00:10:47] Jordan: Dedicated is contractual — monthly or annual reserved capacity. Typical commits start at a few hundred GPU hours/month for mid-enterprise. Latency SLOs depend on model and configuration but we back Dedicated with tighter SLOs and can instrument tail-latency guarantees in contract. We'll include ranges in the pricing doc.
[00:11:10] Sophie: If we need KMS integration, how fast can that be provisioned for a POC?
[00:11:15] Priya: For Dedicated it can be days to provision KMS and networking once contracts are done; for POC we can emulate no-retention and strict access controls on hosted to run an initial benchmark.

[00:11:40] Marta: Can you show retry headers and logs example?
[00:11:44] Priya: Sure — (scrolls) here's a log entry: request_id, client_request_id, attempt=1, latency_ms, status=partial_stream, then final status=ok. We also surface trace IDs. That helps reconcile duplicates during retries.

[00:12:10] Ethan: Any known caveats with streaming large outputs? Our summary job may be 800-1200 tokens sometimes.
[00:12:16] Priya: For long outputs we recommend chunked rendering and monitoring memory usage client-side. On the server side, larger outputs increase KV cache usage; our runtime handles that but cost per request scales. If you often need long summaries, using a larger model with longer context windows or a condensed retrieval+generate pipeline may be more cost-effective.

[00:12:45] Jordan: We're going to flash the sample POC plan in the chat — it's a two-arm test: hosted baseline vs hosted with Optimize batching vs Dedicated. We'll measure latency, cost, and quality on your sample prompts.

[00:13:10] Priya: Demo wrap-up: key takeaways — streaming supported end-to-end; use low temp, stop tokens, and model pinning for deterministic templates; client-side idempotency and SDK backoff for retries; Optimize and console tools to tune batching and cost.

[00:13:30] --- Customer Q&A / Closing ---
[00:13:30] Marta: Is there any additional information you need from us now?
[00:13:33] Jordan: We'll need the sample prompt set and expected outputs, estimated QPS, and preferred date for the POC run. Also let us know if you need a BA/contract template early for PHI.
[00:13:44] Ethan: We'll share prompts and target QPS by tomorrow. One more thing: how do you handle SDK version upgrades that might affect streaming semantics?
[00:13:52] Priya: We document breaking changes and pin SDK compatibility in the release notes. Console rollouts can route older requests to a pinned model version during transitions.

[00:14:10] Jordan: Ok, recap of next steps — Jordan will send pricing and security docs, Priya will schedule the POC and request prompt examples, Aurora to share prompt set and QPS.
[00:14:21] Marta: Great, thanks everyone.
[00:14:24] Ethan: Thanks.
[00:14:26] Sophie: Thanks, bye.

[00:14:30] End of recorded transcript (note: recording ended early at ~14m mark; remaining discussion moved to private chat for procurement).

Notes on transcription: speaker labels are best-effort; some names mis-attributed by auto-transcript. There was a short private procurement discussion after recording stopped.
